name: Question 6
problem: Consider the plane curve $(x-y)^{2}=2x-y.$ Find a tangent vector to that curve at the point $(2,0).$
worked_solution:
First, we bring all variables to one side:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-y)^{2} & =2x-y \\ (x-y)^{2}-2x+y & =0\end{aligned}
$$

If we set $f(x,y)=(x-y)^{2}-2x+y$, our curve can be viewed as the level curve $f(x,y)=0.$ 

A tangent vector to the level curve that passes through the point $(2,0)$ can be computed as follows:

$$
t(2,0)={f}_{y}(2,0)i-{f}_{x}(2,0)j
$$

So, we calculate $t(x,y)$ and evaluate it at $(2,0):$

$$
\begin{aligned}t(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}((x-y)^{2}-2x+y)i-\frac{∂}{∂x}((x-y)^{2}-2x+y)j \\  & =(-2(x-y)+1)i-(2(x-y)-2)j \\ t(2,0) & =(-2((2)-(0))+1)\,i-((2((2)-(0))-2)\,j \\  & =-3\,i-2\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our tangent vector is $-3\,i-2\,j.$

Question 6
?

Consider the plane curve (x−y)2=2x−y. Find a tangent vector to that curve at the point (2,0).

a
−2i−5j
b
−3i−2j
c
2i−3j
d
−5i−4j
e
6i+5j
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we bring all variables to one side: (x−y)2=2x−y(x−y)2−2x+y=0

If we set f(x,y)=(x−y)2−2x+y, our curve can be viewed as the level curve f(x,y)=0.

A tangent vector to the level curve that passes through the point (2,0) can be computed as follows: t(2,0)=fy(2,0)i−fx(2,0)j

So, we calculate t(x,y) and evaluate it at (2,0):

t(x,y)=∂∂y((x−y)2−2x+y)i−∂∂x((x−y)2−2x+y)j=(−2(x−y)+1)i−(2(x−y)−2)jt(2,0)=(−2((2)−(0))+1)i−((2((2)−(0))−2)j=−3i−2j

Therefore, our tangent vector is −3i−2j.
